cards.text: Friend, Jesus just gave some hard teaching, and a lot of His disciples walked away. After this, Jesus travels all around Galilee. But there's one region He's staying out of: Judea.

cards.question: Why doesn't Jesus want to travel in Judea?

answers.text: The Jews there were trying to kill Him
Herod had banned Him from the region
A famine had spread across the land

cards.text: But the Jewish Feast of Tabernacles is near. And here come Jesus' brothers with ADVICE, because a holiday is coming and family ALWAYS has advice.

cards.question: With the feast coming, Jesus' brothers tell Him to leave Galilee and go to ___.
Why do Jesus' brothers want Him to go to Judea?

answers.text: So His disciples there can see His works
So He can make peace with the leaders
So He can teach in the synagogues there

cards.text: Their pitch: "For no one who wants to be known publicly acts in secret. Since You are doing these things, show Yourself to the world." Listen to them, friend. They're talking like a manager who just printed business cards. "Baby, we gotta get you SEEN!"

cards.question: Then John adds a quiet note about Jesus' brothers. True or false: His own brothers believed in Him.

cards.text: Jesus answers His brothers. And He is NOT being rushed. Me? One rattle of that junk drawer and I'd be up yelling "IS IT TIME? IS IT TIME?" Not Him.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus tells His brothers that His time has already come.
Jesus tells His brothers the world can't hate them, but it hates Him. Why does He say it hates Him?

answers.text: He testifies that its works are evil
He takes its crowds away from it

cards.text: Then Jesus tells them, "Go up to the feast on your own." He says He's not going up to this feast, because His time has not yet come.

cards.question: True or false: After telling His brothers this, Jesus stays behind in Galilee.
Once His brothers have gone up to the feast, Jesus goes up too. How does He go?

answers.text: Riding in on a young donkey

cards.text: So at the feast, the Jews are looking for Him and asking, "Where is He?" Friend, I KNOW that question. Years in a junk drawer, I heard it every time somebody dug around for the scissors.

cards.question: Many in the crowds at the feast are whispering about Jesus. What are they saying?

answers.text: Some call Him good and others a deceiver
All of them call Him the promised Messiah
All of them call Him a prophet from God

cards.question: The crowds are whispering, yet no one would speak ___ about Jesus for fear of the Jews.

cards.text: And that's where we'll leave it for now, friend. Keep that oven warm, because this feast is just getting started.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 8 quotes "IS IT TIME? IS IT TIME?", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The opening line states a Bible fact from outside the passage: Jesus gave hard teaching and many disciples walked away (John 6:60, 66). The card gives no reference for it and cites only John 7:1.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The story card runs to about five sentences: the two-sentence quote, "Listen to them, friend," the manager comparison and the made-up "Baby, we gotta get you SEEN!" line. Non-opening story cards are capped at 1 to 2 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: John is brought in as the one adding a note, but the card doesn't say who he is (the writer of this Gospel) the first time he shows up.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The story card runs to about five sentences ("Jesus answers His brothers. And He is NOT being rushed. Me? One rattle... Not Him."). Non-opening story cards are capped at 1 to 2 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The setup gives away card 9. "He is NOT being rushed," the "IS IT TIME?" joke and "Not Him" signal that Jesus says His time hasn't come. That rules out "True" before the baker answers whether His time has already come.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: the setup with the quote, "Friend, I KNOW that question." and the junk drawer line. Non-opening story cards are capped at 1 to 2 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The right answer stands out. Both wrong answers share the "All of them call Him..." pattern, while the right answer alone is built as "Some... and others...", so it's easy to spot without knowing the text.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: The question's own setup ("The crowds are whispering, yet no one would speak ___") rules out both wrong answers. Whispering already is speaking quietly and privately, so "yet" leaves "publicly" as the only answer that makes sense.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The last story card is only the story-continues line and tells no verse content, but it cites John 7:13, which card 16 already covered. The docs allow a last card that is just this line but don't say what such a card should cite.
findings.question: When the last story card is only the story-continues line, what should its "verses" field cite: the passage's last verse, the whole stop's range, or something else?
